raw_response:
I farm only 7 mu, so I cannot spread myself too thin. At home some people go out to work, so I mainly keep to what I know. On about 5 mu I will keep the wheat-maize rotation, because that is the steady way here and it gives grain in two seasons. The other 2 mu I will keep in cotton. Cotton takes more looking after, but if the price is decent it helps with cash. I do not read those technical things, so I do it mostly the old way: look at the field, ask around, and follow what worked in past years. If the crop looks weak, I would rather spend a bit more on fertilizer than lose yield, but I still cannot spend too hard because cash must stay in hand.

For wheat, I will sow in early October like usual, using the local seed people around here use. I will put most fertilizer before sowing, then add one more time around jointing if the leaves are not dark enough. With well water, I plan a few irrigations, but not too many because pumping costs money. After wheat comes off, maize has to go in quickly, so I will not do fancy tillage, just simple turning and sow right away. For cotton, I will keep only a small patch because it needs more watching and more spraying, and my family labor is not always free.
